analysis.title: Micron Technology, Inc Investor Meetings: Memory's strategic value and cycle durability only rising
key_insights: BofA maintains Buy and top-pick status on Micron (MU) with a $1,550 price objective (stock at $877.55) after investor meetings with the COO, CTO, CFO and IR head in New York and Boston, following MU's Tech and Product webinar.
BofA is incrementally more positive on memory after the meetings. Management increasingly sees CY27 and CY28 as tighter than CY26.
Management reads the current memory de-spec (GPU vendors and hyperscalers specifying less memory per system) as evidence of memory shortages, not of compute, land, power or shell constraints.

GPU vendors and hyperscalers have incentives to de-spec memory now, because compute economics are attractive and logic/CoWoS capacity is more available, and they want to fully monetize it even with less memory initially. If memory becomes available, system builders could re-spec memory upward, since it is the largest contributor to token/$ and ROI.

Strategic Customer Agreements (SCAs) span about 5 years, extending beyond CY30 with CY31 discussions underway, versus historical long-term agreements with visibility of 1 year or less. This lets MU forecast bit demand 3-5 years out and cut capex or tool spend in advance if demand slows.

All SCAs are take-or-pay with committed bit volumes and financial commitments. About 35% of total sales are expected to be covered by SCAs, with a target of about 50% by CY30. The pricing framework has a price floor well above the prior cycle high.
MU flagged support for HBM 4-hi through 16-hi, custom HBM, vHBM (a potential scalable alternative to SRAM) and vEIM (for edge applications).

MU expects four more planar DRAM nodes after 1-gamma, with the 1-delta volume ramp targeted for 2H27. Management downplayed 4F² DRAM, saying capacitor scaling matters more than cell footprint and that no customers have shown interest in 4F².
In NAND, G11 targets 400+ layers and twice G9's bits by the end of CY27. MU is developing both SLC and TSV-enabled NAND, with adoption depending on customer interest.

Management reiterated its intent to increase share repurchases using prior-quarter free cash flow beginning Dec-9, the CHIPS restriction deadline. About $35bn is currently authorized, and further authorization needs board approval. BofA estimates about $150-200bn a year of FCF in CY27-28.

market_movers.rationale: Maintains Buy and top pick on the strategic value of memory and longer, take-or-pay SCAs that reduce cycle volatility. Price objective is a sum-of-parts: $1,127/sh for traditional memory at 3.0x CY28E P/B and $422/sh for AI HBM at 21x CY28E P/E.

sector_views.rationale: Memory is increasingly the key enabler of AI performance, token/$ and power efficiency. Management sees CY27/28 tighter than CY26, and multi-year take-or-pay SCAs add supply flexibility.

earnings_insights: BofA estimates MU free cash flow of about $150-200bn a year in CY27-28 (BofA estimate, not reported). Management intends to raise buybacks from the prior quarter's FCF starting Dec-9.
BofA's valuation uses CY28E P/B of 3.0x for the traditional memory business and CY28E P/E of 21x for the AI HBM business (BofA estimates). ROE for 2027E is 95.8% (BofA estimate).

trade_ideas.rationale: Mid- and longer-term strategic value of memory and cycle durability from multi-year take-or-pay SCAs.
trade_ideas.risk: Larger than expected memory ASP decline, greater competition from China newcomers, share loss to large competitors, softening demand across data center, smartphones or PCs.

risk_factors: Larger than expected memory ASP decline.
Softening demand across major end markets such as data center, smartphones or PCs.
geopolitical: The CHIPS restriction deadline of Dec-9 limits MU's share repurchases until then.
